title: Attracting subgroups and a big cell for a multiplicative-group automorphism action over a field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and $H$ a smooth geometrically connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $a:\mathbf G_m\times_k H\to H$ be an action by group-scheme automorphisms [def-sc-gm-ga]: $a(1,h)=h$, $a(st,h)=a(s,a(t,h))$ and $a(t,hh')=a(t,h)a(t,h')$ on all test algebras. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ define $U_+(A)$ to be the $h\in H(A)$ such that $t\mapsto a(t,h)$ extends to an $A$-morphism $\mathbf A^1_A\to H_A$ taking $0$ to the identity; define $U_-(A)$ by the same condition on $t\mapsto a(t^{-1},h)$. Here $H_A$ is scalar extension and $\mathbf A^1_A=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$. The functors $U_+$ and $U_-$ are represented by smooth geometrically connected closed $a$-stable $k$-subgroups of $H$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Put $\mathfrak h=T_1H$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] and $\mathfrak h_j=\{v:a(t)v=t^jv\}$, where equality is required after every commutative algebra extension. Then $\operatorname{Lie}(U_+)=\bigoplus_{j>0}\mathfrak h_j$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(U_-)=\bigoplus_{j<0}\mathfrak h_j$, equivariantly for $a$. If $\mathfrak h_0=0$, multiplication $U_-\times_k U_+\to H$ is an open immersion with dense image [def-weil-open-immersion]. Density means density of the image in the underlying topological space. Both assertions include the trivial group and arbitrary characteristic; no perfectness assumption is made.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(a)-(e), printed pp.265-266, applied to the semidirect product H semidirect G_m with its distinguished cocharacter; definitions 13.29-13.30, pp.263-265. The final big-cell assertion is the zero-fixed-tangent specialization, obtained from the smooth connected centralizer and the open multiplication map in (b),(d); this is an agent-extracted automorphism-action form, not Proposition 16.63.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] to the coordinate algebra of $H$: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus the affine finite-type group $H$ is finitely presented, as required by [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups]. Apply that node over $R=k$ to $a$ and to $-a(t,h)=a(t^{-1},h)$. Its functors on every commutative test algebra are exactly the two functors in the item. It supplies smooth geometrically connected closed subgroups $U_+,U_-$ and the equalities $T_1U_+=\bigoplus_{j>0}\mathfrak h_j$, $T_1U_-=\bigoplus_{j<0}\mathfrak h_j$: the reciprocal action replaces character $j$ by $-j$. Also retain its smooth geometrically connected fixed subgroup $Z=Z_a$, limit subgroup $P=P_a$, equality $T_1Z=\mathfrak h_0$, and scheme isomorphism $Z\times U_+\simeq P$ given by multiplication. The geometric connectedness clauses apply because $H$ is geometrically connected; the node expressly permits arbitrary base change.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(a)-(c),(e), pp.265-266, automorphism-action form; existing relative dynamic-subgroup theorem supplies this general form.

proof.text: For every $A$, let $F_h(s)\in H(A[s])$ be the extension belonging to $h\in U_+(A)$. It is unique because the coordinate restriction $A[s]\to A[s,s^{-1}]$ is injective. For $t\in A^\times$, the morphism $s\mapsto a(t,F_h(s))$ extends the orbit of $a(t,h)$: for invertible $s$, $a(s,a(t,h))=a(t,a(s,h))$. Its value at zero is $a(t,1)=1$. Therefore $a(t,h)\in U_+(A)$, naturally in $A$; the same calculation for $a(s^{-1},h)$ proves stability of $U_-$. Apply this natural rule to the universal point of the affine scheme $\mathbf G_m\times U_\pm$ to obtain the restricted action morphism, and compose with the closed inclusion to check its action identities. Differentiating these commuting inclusion diagrams gives equivariance of the tangent identifications in step 1; in dual-number terms both maps simply apply $a(t,-)$ to the same infinitesimal point. The natural injective tangent maps for closed subgroup inclusions are supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus].

source.place: Propositions 13.29-13.30 and Theorem 13.33(c), pp.264-266; stability and equivariance checked on all test algebras.

proof.text: Now suppose $\mathfrak h_0=0$. The group $Z$ of step 1 is smooth, geometrically connected, affine and finite type, has the rational identity point, and satisfies $T_1Z=0$. Equip it with the trivial $\mathbf G_m$ action. The positive-weight hypothesis of [lem-sfb-positive-weight-affine-space-arbitrary-field] is satisfied by the empty direct sum of weight spaces. Its zero-dimensional clause gives $Z\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$, carrying the identity to its sole point. Hence $Z(A)$ has exactly its identity element for every $A$, including nonreduced algebras. This is triviality as a group scheme, not just triviality of its geometric points.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, pp.269-270, empty-tangent case; applied to the fixed subgroup from Theorem 13.33(a),(c),(e).

proof.text: The isomorphism $Z\times U_+\to P$ of step 1 now has source $U_+$, and its map is $u\mapsto1u=u$ in $H(A)$ for every $A$. It therefore identifies the actual subgroup inclusion $U_+\hookrightarrow H$ with $P\hookrightarrow H$. Substitute this identification in the open immersion $U_{-a}\times P_a\to H$ of [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups]. Since $U_{-a}=U_-$ by the defining orbit formula, the resulting morphism is precisely $(u_-,u_+)\mapsto u_-u_+$, proving the requested open immersion. Its image contains the identity.

The underlying space of $H$ is nonempty, because it has its identity, and connected, because it is geometrically connected. Smoothness gives regularity by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]; [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] then makes $H$ integral. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], its space is irreducible. The image in step 4 is a nonempty open subset by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Every nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is dense: otherwise the nonempty open complement of its closure would be disjoint from it, contrary to irreducibility. This is precisely density in the underlying topological space required in the item.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(d)-(e), p.266; regular connected scheme geometry for density.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q35-10aafb13a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First split of the item; the base proof was empty, so this is not a 2026-10-21 re-split. The statement is unchanged and there are no new nodes. I read all five steps against the cited statements. Step 1: a field is Noetherian, so the finite-type affine H is finitely presented (Stacks 00FP); lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups over R=k then gives U_+=U_a and U_-=U_{-a} as the item defines them. The U_a geometric fibres are connected, so U_± are geometrically connected, and Z and P are geometrically connected because H is. It also gives the Lie clauses, with the reciprocal action turning j into -j. Step 2: stability is proved by an explicit orbit calculation, a(ts,h)=a(s,a(t,h)) with value a(t,1)=1 at s=0. The extension is unique because A[s] embeds in A[s,s^{-1}], and the dual-number calculus node supplies the injective tangent maps for equivariance. Step 3: h_0=0 gives T_1Z=0. Z is smooth, geometrically connected, affine and of finite type, and its identity is fixed by the trivial action, so the empty-weight (d=0) clause of lem-sfb-positive-weight-affine-space-arbitrary-field gives Z≅Spec k (matches Milne 13.41). Step 4: with Z trivial, the isomorphism Z⋉U_+≅P, (z,u)↦zu, makes U_+=P. The open immersion U_{-a}×P_a→H then becomes exactly multiplication (u_-,u_+)↦u_-u_+ in the stated order. Step 5: smooth gives regular; regular, nonempty and connected gives integral, hence irreducible; a nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is dense. I checked Milne iAG2017 Thm 13.33(a)-(e), pp.265-266, and Thm 13.41/Def 13.40, pp.269-270, in the local PDF. Small cases, all consistent: H=1; G_a with weight n>0 and n<0; G_a^2 with weights ±1; GL_2 under diag(t,t^{-1}), where h_0≠0 so no big-cell claim; weight p in characteristic p. Batch-5 check: the cited positive-weight node reaches lem-trf-polynomial-nonzero-ideal-quotient-dimension-bound, which says dim k[t_1..t_n]/I ≤ n-1 for nonzero I (Stacks 00QK). That is a general Krull-dimension fact, outside both the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions and not specific to their proofs, so I accept it. The three tool_uses (Noetherian finite type gives finite presentation, smooth over a field gives regular, regular connected gives integral) are generic scheme facts and are accepted. proof_deps is the union of the uses. No changes made.
